newsitem.title: USA: Mexico to import more corn, wheat in 97/98-Attache.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to import more corn, wheat in 97/98-Attache.

text.p: Mexico will import more corn, wheat and sorghum in 1997/98 than this marketing year and most of the imports will be U.S. grain, the U.S. attache in Mexico City said in a report released Friday.

The attache lowered his forecast for corn import in 1996/97 to 3.7 million tonnes because of a good domestic crop. The forecast had been 4.2 million tonnes. For 1997/98, imports were pegged at 4.3 million tonnes, all from the United States.

Wheat imports were forecast for 1.6 million tonnes in 1996/97, down from an earlier estimate of 2.07 million tonnes due to lower consumption. For 1997/98, imports would be 1.68 million tonnes, 1.4 million of it U.S. wheat, the report said.

The forecast for sorghum imports in 1996/97 also was lowered, to 1.1 million tonnes, down 200,000. For 1997/98, imports were forecast at 1.2 million tonnes. The United States would supply all of the imports in both marketing years.
